From Zero to JLPT N5: An Adaptive Beginner Plan

Kanjidon Team · Feb 22, 2026

This is an adaptive study framework, not the story of an invented learner and not a promise that one product produces an N5 result. Start from your actual baseline, collect evidence from fresh tasks and expand the plan only when the current layer works.

What N5 Covers

The official JLPT describes N5 as the ability to understand some basic Japanese. The test includes language knowledge, reading and listening. It does not directly assess conversation or handwriting, so add those skills when they matter to your real-world goal.

Foundation A: Kana and Sound

  • Learn hiragana and katakana through words, not only chart order.
  • Connect each spelling to audio and practise decoding unfamiliar combinations.
  • Use romaji only as temporary support and remove it as soon as it stops helping.
  • Notice long vowels, small kana and doubled consonants in both reading and listening.

Foundation B: Useful Words, Grammar and Kanji

Build short sentences around high-utility words and basic grammar. Introduce kanji inside those words, with the reading used there, rather than memorizing every possible reading of an isolated character. The JLPT does not provide a fixed N5 kanji inventory, so third-party totals are planning conventions, not official boundaries.

Foundation C: Reading and Listening

  • Read short notices, messages and descriptions for the main idea before translating details.
  • Listen to brief exchanges and identify who is doing what, where and when.
  • Repeat with a transcript after the first attempt, then listen again without it.
  • Track whether errors come from vocabulary, grammar, script decoding or missed audio cues.

A Sustainable Study Cycle

StepActionEvidence
LearnAdd a small connected set of words and one sentence patternYou can explain and use the target without copying
RetrieveRecall meaning or reading before revealing the answerFailures are graded honestly and corrected
ApplyRead or hear the targets in a fresh contextThe material is recognized outside the lesson
DiagnoseClassify mistakes by skillThe next cycle addresses the actual weakness

Check Readiness with Official Material

Use the official N5 samples after building a foundation. Work untimed first to separate comprehension from speed, then try the official format. A total score from one familiar set is less useful than an error log showing which question types and language features still fail.

Official JLPT Sources

  • Official JLPT description of the linguistic competence required at each level
  • Official JLPT sample questions and practice workbooks
  • Official JLPT FAQ on test content, scoring and published lists
